plugins.name: cloudflare
plugins.description: Cloudflare stack plugin for vwf â **scope is deliberately parked**. Workers, Pages, R2, D1, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, Images and Stream are **not** offered yet and arrive under their own dedicated plan â so the menu says what it does not cover rather than coming back quietly short. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: datastore
plugins.description: Datastore capability plugin for vwf â the neutral contract every datastore must satisfy (write versioning, transactional multi-record writes, server-generated time, the services-layer access rule, a deterministic local stack) plus the one provider that needs no cloud: **PostgreSQL**, self-hosted or managed anywhere. Managed flavours â Firestore, Cloud SQL, and the rest â come from the project's own cloud plugin, not from here. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: design-tools
plugins.description: Carrier for the Claude Design MCP server only. Its three design-adapter skills merged into vwf; this manifest survives solely because an MCP server is a plugin-manifest feature no repo file can express, and it retires once stackgen can generate that wiring on demand.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: devtools
plugins.description: The developer-machine toolchain in one plugin â mise (the .config/ three-file MISE_ENV split, tool/env placement, the file-based task library, the CI node-gpg workaround) plus /devtools:scaffold and the repo-level quality gates: dprint, ESLint, gitleaks, grype, pre-commit. Its stack adapter retired in Wave C, its Docker/OCI doctrine in Wave D and its Doppler doctrine with the secrets-manager packs â the deploy artifact is now stackgen's container-image pack, the local stack its harness contract, and secrets a user-picked provider on the backing axis. This plugin holds no secrets doctrine at all.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: flutter
plugins.description: Opinionated Flutter plugin â a `dart` router skill (lean SKILL.md routing to on-demand references: GetX, a Firebase suite of auth/analytics/app-check/crashlytics/messaging/storage, and feature areas of architecture, state, navigation, theming, layouts, animations, performance, maps, webview, webrtc, revenuecat, image handling, http/json, concurrency, caching, testing, flavors, app-size, coverage, build) and a `swift` router skill (Swift, SwiftUI, Xcode), plus `kotlin`, `pubspec`, `analysis-options`, and `internationalization`, and bundled Dart, Kotlin & Swift (SourceKit) language servers. Its stack adapter retired in Wave C â `dart-flutter` is a stackgen bundle now, and the app-framework pack carries the Dart/Kotlin/Swift judgment. Self-contained â no cross-marketplace dependencies.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: gcp
plugins.description: Google Cloud stack plugin for vwf â the judgment layer an SDK reference cannot give you: which service to pick and when it stops being the answer, how each one bills and the traps that multiply it, which services have local emulators (and where they lie), and least-privilege IAM shapes. Covers the full Firebase suite plus Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Memorystore, Bigtable, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Scheduler, Eventarc, Workflows, Cloud Storage, Cloud Run, GKE, Artifact Registry, Cloud Deploy, Cloud Armor, VPC, DNS, Load Balancing, CDN, KMS, Backup & DR, reCAPTCHA Enterprise and Vertex AI. Observability is OpenTelemetry only â GCP services appear as OTLP sinks, never as vendor SDKs. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: identity
plugins.description: Identity capability plugin for vwf â the neutral contract every identity provider must satisfy (token verification at the edge of every authenticated route, what a token claim may and may not carry, session and revocation shape, the operator plane) plus the one provider that belongs to no cloud: any **OIDC** issuer, self-hosted or managed. Managed flavours â Firebase Auth, Identity Platform, and the rest â come from the project's own cloud plugin, not from here. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: object-storage
plugins.description: Object-storage capability plugin for vwf â **contract only, and deliberately so**. It owns the neutral vocabulary and requirements (buckets, object lifecycle, signed access, retention, the never-proxy-bytes rule) and ships **no provider of its own**: every object store worth using is a cloud's, so the flavour comes from the project's cloud plugin â Cloud Storage from `gcp`, R2 from `cloudflare` once that plugin is unparked. Its menu says that out loud rather than coming back empty, because an empty menu is indistinguishable from a broken adapter. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: observability
plugins.description: Observability capability plugin for vwf â the neutral contract every telemetry backend must satisfy (the product emits **OTLP** and never a vendor SDK, one correlated trace/metric/log story, cardinality as a design decision, retention and cost) plus the self-hosted sink that needs no cloud: **OpenTelemetry into a Grafana OTel-LGTM stack**. Managed flavours â Cloud Monitoring and the rest â come from the project's own cloud plugin, and appear only as OTLP destinations. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: orchestration
plugins.description: Async orchestration capability plugin for vwf â the neutral contract every durable-work backend must satisfy (at-least-once delivery and the idempotency it forces, retry and back-off discipline, the poison-message path, visibility into work in flight) plus the self-hosted engine that belongs to no cloud: **Temporal**. Managed flavours â Cloud Workflows, Pub/Sub, task queues and the rest â come from the project's own cloud plugin, not from here. Implements the vwf stack-adapter contract.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: stackgen
plugins.description: The principles-driven stack materializer â implements the vwf stack-adapter contract with a dispatch rule: a technology a shipped pack covers is copied from the pack; anything uncovered is generated (Context7 research â vwf's principles catalog â the stackgen-skill-reviewer gate). Both paths land directly in the repo's committed .claude/ tree â skills, agents, hooks and rules only, structured per a closed kind vocabulary, recorded in a lockfile â editable and plugin-independent for collaborators. Re-sync is explicit and diffed, never silent. Waves AâC landed 21 packs and 19 bundles across seven kinds; Wave D adds the eighth kind, deploy-target, whose container-image pack is the curated answer the container-generic bundle used to generate, assets/artifact-doctrine.md â the host rules deciding whether a generated skill, agent or hook is valid at all â and the ninth kind, design-tool, whose three packs land vwf's design adapters at fixed names in the repo's own .claude/. Two tool axes (design, cicd) let a pack be reached by the config token that selects it, which is what rescued a CI pack no menu could offer. The secrets-manager category then landed on the backing axis behind assets/contracts/secrets.md, where the whole decision is where the secret lives and what onboarding a teammate costs â and where devtools' Doppler doctrine went.
plugins.author: Viraj Patel

plugins.name: typescript
plugins.description: The TypeScript language plugin â one plugin per toolchain, this one owning the Node/TS ecosystem and so covering both `typescript` and `javascript`. A `typescript` router skill (lean SKILL.md routing to on-demand references: the coding standards baseline, Vitest testing, the build pipeline for single-package and monorepo) plus an `effect` router skill for Effect-TS doctrine, `package-json`, `pnpm`, `tsconfig`, `lint-format`, and the TypeScript/JavaScript language server. plugins.name: modo-tdah
plugins.description: Dois modos de saida para leitor com TDAH: acao primeiro (EXECUTAR) ou resposta primeiro (ENTENDER).
plugins.author: Rafael Marchetti

plugins.name: aerospace-engineering
plugins.description: Aerospace Engineering: aerodynamics fundamentals and how lift actually works, airfoils and wings, the drag breakdown, compressible and supersonic flow, aircraft performance, stability and control, air-breathing propulsion, structures and materials, aeroelasticity, flight controls and avionics, drones and UAS including multirotor dynamics and the regulatory picture, launch vehicles, flight test and certification, and the design process.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: agile-delivery
plugins.description: Agile Delivery: Security-First Scrum methodology, evidence-based delivery velocity, and engineering metrics.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: ai-and-data
plugins.description: AI and Data Engineering: data pipelines and warehousing, AI/ML landscape and production patterns, RAG and AI agent development, and LLM token and cost optimization on Azure (including provider-agnostic prompt/context compression).
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: ai-chatbot-strategy
plugins.description: AI Chatbot Strategy: foundational AI and chatbot concepts for business, RAG architecture explained for non-technical decision-makers, custom chatbot build and deployment guide, and chatbot business value with ROI frameworks.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: algorithms-deep-dive
plugins.description: Algorithms Deep Dive: choosing and reasoning about algorithms and data structures, the machine model that makes asymptotic analysis lie (cache, branches, allocation, SIMD), the core data structure families, hash tables and modern probing, trees and the B-tree/LSM storage divide, sorting as it is actually implemented today, searching and indexing, graphs, strings, dynamic programming and amortization, probabilistic and streaming structures, vector and similarity search, concurrent data structures, and the measurement discipline that separates real optimization from folklore.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: arm-architecture-deep-dive
plugins.description: ARM â A Deep Dive: what "ARM" actually names, the licensing model, product families, ISA generations, AArch64, instruction set characteristics, exception levels, the memory model, MMU and translation, vector extensions including NEON, SVE, SVE2 and SME, atomics and synchronization, floating point and numerics, TrustZone, pointer authentication, BTI and MTE, CCA and realms, big.LITTLE and DynamIQ, interrupts and timers, interconnect, boot and firmware, virtualization, Cortex-M and embedded, toolchain and ABI, porting from x86, and performance analysis.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: art-theory-fundamentals
plugins.description: Art Theory Fundamentals: what kind of claim art theory actually makes, the formal elements, value, colour, composition, pictorial space, medium and materiality, the philosophical questions, beauty and the sublime, taste and judgement, theories of art and the definition problem, art and ethics, a historical skeleton from modernism to contemporary, the canon problem, iconography and iconology, semiotics, critical lenses, intention and the author, how to actually look at a work, and the art world and market.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: assembly-programming
plugins.description: Assembly Programming: instruction-level reference for x86-64, AArch64, and RISC-V â the machine model, calling conventions and ABIs, assemblers and toolchains, reading disassembly, performance engineering, SIMD/vector (SSE/AVX/AVX-512, NEON/SVE2/SME, RVV), systems and constant-time cryptographic assembly, inline assembly and intrinsics, and debugging/verification.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: automotive-software
plugins.description: Automotive Software: what makes vehicle software different, E/E architecture and the shift to zonal and central compute, buses and networking (CAN and its details, Automotive Ethernet and service-oriented communication), AUTOSAR Classic and Adaptive, real-time scheduling, functional safety under ISO 26262 including ASIL determination and decomposition and SOTIF, cybersecurity under ISO/SAE 21434 and the UN R155 and R156 regulations, diagnostics, flashing and OTA, ADAS and autonomy, process and toolchain, testing, the vehicle domains, and supply chain reality.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: aws-gcp-azure-deep-dive
plugins.description: AWS, GCP and Azure Deep Dive: an honest framing of what actually differs between the three, shared responsibility, identity and access where the providers genuinely diverge, resource hierarchy and organization, networking, compute, containers and Kubernetes, serverless, storage, databases, analytics, AI/ML services, observability, cost mechanics, reliability, regions and SLAs, infrastructure as code, lock-in and multi-cloud assessed honestly, migration, and a service equivalence mapping.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: azure-cloud-infra
plugins.description: Azure Cloud Infrastructure: Azure RBAC administration, Kubernetes IaC with GitOps/Helm/Terraform, and Azure service catalog with production decision guide for compute, messaging, networking, and AI.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: banking-swift-and-payment-networks
plugins.description: Banking, SWIFT and Payment Networks: what a payment actually is, what a bank is and how deposits are created, central banks and reserves, the payment system taxonomy, clearing, netting and settlement risk, correspondent banking, what SWIFT actually is, message formats from MT to ISO 20022, gpi and tracking, governance, sanctions and geopolitics, alternatives and parallel systems, Ripple versus XRP versus the XRP Ledger, XRP Ledger mechanics, Ripple's products, legal status, instant payment systems, stablecoins, CBDCs, tokenized deposits, compliance, security, and the costs and economics of remittances.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: biology-chemistry-foundations
plugins.description: Biology and Chemistry Foundations: atoms and periodicity, bonding and molecular geometry, intermolecular forces, phases and solutions, thermodynamics, kinetics, equilibrium and acid-base chemistry, redox and electrochemistry, organic chemistry and reaction mechanism, analytical methods and spectroscopy, biomolecules, enzymes, bioenergetics and metabolism, membranes and transport, cell architecture, the cell cycle and signalling, and evolution â the chemistry and biology a technical reader actually needs, with the reasoning that transfers.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: biomedical-engineering-technical
plugins.description: Biomedical Engineering: physiological signal processing, medical imaging modality physics and DICOM internals, clinical data structures, the technicals of clinical machine learning (prevalence, calibration, shortcut learning, the validation ladder), bioinformatics, structural and systems biology, PK/PD, physiological modelling, biomechanics, biomaterials, tissue engineering, neural interfaces and prosthetics, lab automation and instrumentation, and the biostatistics that determine whether any of it holds up.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: business-marketing-sales-law
plugins.description: Business, Marketing, Sales and Law: business models and unit economics, strategy, operations and organization, financing, marketing fundamentals and what the evidence actually shows, brand and advertising, measurement and attribution, channels, the sales process, qualification, negotiation, sales management, and a deliberately scoped commercial-law layer covering how legal risk materializes, contracts, intellectual property, employment, privacy and data, consumer protection and marketing law, and disputes.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: cad-3d-printing
plugins.description: CAD and 3D Printing: geometry representations and kernels, file formats and what each one loses, code-CAD and scripting including the OpenSCAD versus OCCT trade, mesh processing and repair, the slicing pipeline and G-code, the additive processes and the physics that determines part quality, design for additive manufacturing, tolerances and fits, materials, generative design and lattices, automation pipelines, and scanning and reverse engineering.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: calculus-geometry-algebra
plugins.description: Calculus, Geometry and Algebra: vector spaces and linear maps, matrices and the four fundamental subspaces, determinants, eigenvalues and diagonalization, inner products and orthogonality, the spectral theorem and SVD, matrix factorizations, conditioning and numerical reality, the derivative and integration, series and Taylor approximation, multivariable and vector calculus, differential forms, constrained optimization, differential equations, geometry, manifolds, tensors done properly, Riemannian geometry, and Lie groups and algebras.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger

plugins.name: chaos-theory
plugins.description: Chaos Theory: what chaos actually is and is not, the stretch-and-fold mechanism, dynamical systems, stability and linearization, bifurcations, the logistic map and Feigenbaum universality, Lyapunov exponents, strange attractors, the routes to chaos, fractals and dimension, Poincare sections and symbolic dynamics, Hamiltonian chaos and KAM, detecting chaos in real data, control and synchronization, where chaos actually appears, and computing chaotic systems numerically.
plugins.author: Adam Matthew Steinberger
